title.zh: 卷一百十三 列傳第四十三: 逆臣中
title.raw: 卷一百十三 列傳第四十三: 逆臣中 Volume 113 Biographies 43: Rebellious Officials 2

sentences.zh: 蕭翰耶律牒蠟耶律朗耶律劉哥

translations.literal: Xiao Han, Yelü Diepa, Yelü Lang, Yelü Liuge
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han, Yelü Diepa, Yelü Lang, and Yelü Liuge

translations.literal: (Pendu)〉 (alternate name, closing parenthesis)〉
translations.idiomatic: Pendu)〉

sentences.zh: 耶律海思耶律敵獵蕭革

translations.literal: Yelü Haishi, Yelü Dilie, Xiao Ge
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Haishi, Yelü Dilie, and Xiao Ge

sentences.zh: 蕭翰，一名敵烈，字寒真，宰相敵魯之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Han, also named Dilie, style Hanzhen, was the son of Chancellor Dilu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han, also called Dilie, whose style was Hanzhen, was the son of Chancellor Dilu.

sentences.zh: 天贊初，唐兵圍鎮州，節度使張文禮遣使告急。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianzan, Tang troops besieged Zhen Prefecture, and Military Commissioner Zhang Wenli sent envoys in urgent appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianzan era, Tang forces besieged Zhen Prefecture, and the military commissioner Zhang Wenli sent envoys begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 翰受詔與康末怛往救，克之，殺其將李嗣昭，拔石城。

translations.literal: Han received the edict and went to the rescue with Kang Moda, took the city, killed its general Li Sizhao, and captured Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Han received orders and marched to the rescue with Kang Moda; they took the city, killed the Tang general Li Sizhao, and seized Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 會同初，領漢軍侍衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, he led the Han-army guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huitong era, he commanded the Han-army guard corps.

sentences.zh: 八年，伐晉，敗晉將杜重威，追至望都。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, campaigning against Jin, he defeated the Jin general Du Chongwei and pursued him to Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he campaigned against Jin, routed the Jin general Du Chongwei, and pursued him as far as Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 翰奏曰：「可令軍下馬而射。」

translations.literal: Han memorialized, saying, "The army may be ordered to dismount and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Han submitted a memorial: "Have the army dismount and shoot.

sentences.zh: 帝從其言，軍士步進。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his words, and the soldiers advanced on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice, and the troops advanced on foot.

sentences.zh: 敵人持短兵猝至，我軍失利。

translations.literal: The enemy, bearing short weapons, came suddenly, and our army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy closed in at once with side arms, and our forces were beaten.

sentences.zh: 帝悔之曰：「此吾用言之過至此！」

translations.literal: The Emperor regretted it and said, "This is where taking my words has led!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repented and said, "This is what comes of heeding my own counsel!

sentences.zh: 及從駕入汴，為宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When he followed the imperial procession into Bian, he became Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered Bian, he was made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩欒城，世宗即位。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died at Luancheng, Shizong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Luancheng, Shizong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 翰聞之，委事於李從敏，徑趨行在。

translations.literal: On hearing this, Han entrusted affairs to Li Congmin and went straight to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, Han left his duties to Li Congmin and hurried straight to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，世宗與皇太后相拒於潢河橫渡，和議未定。

translations.literal: That autumn, Shizong and the Empress Dowager confronted each other at Huanghe Hengdu, and peace terms were not settled.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Shizong and the empress dowager faced each other at Huanghe Hengdu, and no settlement had yet been reached.

sentences.zh: 太后問翰曰：「汝何怨而叛？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked Han, "What grievance made you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Han, "What grievance drove you to rebel?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣母無罪，太后殺之，以此不能無憾。」

translations.literal: He replied, "My mother was guiltless, yet Your Majesty killed her; for this I cannot be without resentment."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "My mother was innocent, yet Your Majesty put her to death—for that I cannot be without bitterness."

sentences.zh: 初耶律屋質以附太后被囚，翰聞而快之，即囚所謂曰：「汝嘗言我輩不及，今在狴犴，何也？」

translations.literal: Earlier Yelü Wuzhi had been imprisoned for siding with the Empress Dowager; Han heard of it and rejoiced, and at the prison said to him, "You once said we were not your equal—now you are in the cage; what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yelü Wuzhi had been imprisoned for siding with the empress dowager; when Han heard of it he was delighted, and at the prison he said, "You once claimed we were beneath you—now you sit in a cage; what of that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「第願公不至如此！」

translations.literal: He replied, "I only wish you would not come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi answered, "I only hope you never come to this pass!"

sentences.zh: 翰默然。

translations.literal: Han was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Han said nothing.

sentences.zh: 天祿二年，尚帝妹阿不裏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianlu, he married the Emperor's younger sister Abuli.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianlu he married the emperor's younger sister Abuli.

sentences.zh: 後與天德謀反，下獄。

translations.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Tiande and was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later he conspired to rebel with Tiande and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 復結惕隱劉哥及其弟盆都亂，耶律石剌告屋質，屋持遽入奏之，翰等不伏。

translations.literal: He again joined Tiyin Liuge and his younger brother Pendu in disorder; Yelü Shila informed Wuzhi, and Wuzhi at once entered and reported it; Han and the others would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined with Tiyin Liuge and Liuge's younger brother Pendu in a plot; Yelü Shila reported it to Wuzhi, who rushed in to inform the throne, but Han and his fellows would not confess.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲發其事，屋質固諍以為不可，乃詔屋質鞫按。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to expose the affair; Wuzhi remonstrated firmly that it could not be allowed, and an edict ordered Wuzhi to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to bring the matter to light, but Wuzhi argued strenuously that this could not stand, and the emperor ordered Wuzhi to investigate and try the case.

sentences.zh: 翰伏辜，帝竟釋之。

translations.literal: Han confessed his guilt, yet the Emperor in the end released him.
translations.idiomatic: Han confessed, yet the emperor ultimately set him free.

sentences.zh: 復與公主以書結明王安端反，屋質得其書以奏，翰伏誅。

translations.literal: He again, with the princess by letter, joined Prince Ming'an Anduan in rebellion; Wuzhi obtained the letter and memorialized with it, and Han was executed on confession.
translations.idiomatic: He again conspired with the princess by letter to join Prince Ming'an Anduan in rebellion; Wuzhi obtained the letter and presented it to the throne, and Han was put to death after confessing.

sentences.zh: 劉哥，字明隱，太祖弟寅底石之子。

translations.literal: Liuge, style Mingyin, was the son of Taizu's younger brother Yindishi.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge, whose style was Mingyin, was a son of Taizu's younger brother Yindishi.

sentences.zh: 幼驕狠，好陵侮人，長益凶狡。

translations.literal: As a child he was arrogant and fierce, fond of bullying others; grown, he became all the more vicious and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was arrogant and brutal and loved to bully others; as a man he grew only more savage and cunning.

sentences.zh: 太宗惡之，使守邊僥，累遷西南邊大詳穩。

translations.literal: Taizong disliked him and sent him to guard the frontier of Jiao, and he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Xiangwen of the southwestern border.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong disliked him and posted him to guard the Jiao frontier; he rose through repeated promotions to Grand Xiangwen of the southwestern border.

sentences.zh: 會同十年，叔父安端從帝伐晉，以病先歸，與劉哥鄰居。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Huitong, his uncle Anduan followed the Emperor in the campaign against Jin, returned early on account of illness, and lived as Liuge's neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Huitong his uncle Anduan accompanied the emperor against Jin but came home early with illness and became Liuge's neighbor.

sentences.zh: 世宗立於軍中，安端議所往，劉哥首建附世宗之策，以本部兵助之。

translations.literal: When Shizong was established in the army, Anduan debated where to go; Liuge was the first to propose attaching to Shizong and aided him with his own tribal forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was proclaimed in the army, Anduan debated which side to take; Liuge was first to urge siding with Shizong and supported him with his tribal troops.

sentences.zh: 時太后命皇太弟李胡率兵而南，劉哥、安端遇於泰德泉。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager ordered the Imperial Younger Brother Li Hu to lead troops south; Liuge and Anduan met him at Taide Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had ordered the imperial younger brother Li Hu to march south with an army; Liuge and Anduan met him at Taide Spring.

sentences.zh: 既接戰，安端墜馬。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, Anduan fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, Anduan was thrown from his horse.

sentences.zh: 王子天德馳至，欲以槍刺之。

translations.literal: Prince Tiande galloped up and wished to stab him with a spear.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tiande galloped up and tried to run him through with a spear.

sentences.zh: 劉哥以身衛安端，射天德，貫甲不及膚。

translations.literal: Liuge shielded Anduan with his body, shot Tiande, and the arrow pierced his armor without reaching the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge shielded Anduan with his own body, shot at Tiande, and the arrow pierced his armor without touching his skin.

sentences.zh: 安端得馬復戰，太弟兵敗。

translations.literal: Anduan regained a horse and fought again; the Younger Brother's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Anduan remounted and fought on, and the younger brother's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 劉哥與安端朝於行在。

translations.literal: Liuge and Anduan attended court at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge and Anduan presented themselves at the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，太后問劉哥曰：「汝何怨而叛？」

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, the Empress Dowager asked Liuge, "What grievance made you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, the empress dowager asked Liuge, "What grievance made you rebel?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣父無罪，太后殺之，以此怨耳。」

translations.literal: He replied, "My father was guiltless, yet Your Majesty killed him; for this there is resentment."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "My father was innocent, yet Your Majesty killed him—that is my grievance."

sentences.zh: 事平，以功為惕隱。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, for his merit he was made Tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was made tiyin for his service.

sentences.zh: 天祿中，與其弟盆都、王子天德、侍衛蕭翰謀反，耶律石剌發其事，劉哥以飾辭免。

translations.literal: During Tianlu, with his younger brother Pendu, Prince Tiande, and Guard Xiao Han he plotted rebellion; Yelü Shila exposed the affair, and Liuge escaped by polished excuses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianlu era he plotted rebellion with his younger brother Pendu, Prince Tiande, and the guard Xiao Han; Yelü Shila exposed the plot, but Liuge talked his way free.

sentences.zh: 後請帝博，欲因進酒弒逆，帝覺之，不果，被囚。

translations.literal: Later he asked the Emperor to gamble, intending to assassinate him when presenting wine; the Emperor perceived it, it did not succeed, and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he invited the emperor to gamble, planning to murder him when he served wine; the emperor sensed it, the plot failed, and Liuge was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 一日，召劉哥，鎖項以博。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor summoned Liuge and, with his neck locked, gambled with him.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor summoned Liuge and gambled with him while a collar was locked about his neck.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「汝實反耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked, "Did you truly rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Did you really rebel?

sentences.zh: 劉哥誓曰：「臣若有反心，必生千頂疽死！」

translations.literal: Liuge swore, "If your servant harbors a rebellious heart, may he die of a thousand-headed carbuncle!"
translations.idiomatic: Liuge swore, "If I harbor rebellion in my heart, may I die of the thousand-headed carbuncle!"

sentences.zh: 遂貰之。

translations.literal: He was then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 耶律屋質固諍，以為罪在不赦。

translations.literal: Yelü Wuzhi remonstrated firmly, holding that the crime was unpardonable.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Wuzhi argued strenuously that the offense was beyond pardon.

sentences.zh: 上命屋質按之，具服。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Wuzhi to investigate; Liuge fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wuzhi to investigate, and Liuge confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 詔免死，流烏古部，果以千頂疽死。

translations.literal: An edict spared his life and exiled him to the Wugu tribe; he indeed died of the thousand-headed carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared his life and banished him to the Wugu tribe, where he did in fact die of the thousand-headed carbuncle.

sentences.zh: 弟盆都。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pendu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Pendu.

sentences.zh: 盆都，殘忍多力，膚若蛇皮。

translations.literal: Pendu was cruel and possessed great strength; his skin was like snakeskin.
translations.idiomatic: Pendu was cruel and immensely strong, and his skin resembled snakeskin.

sentences.zh: 天祿初，以族屬為皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianlu, by reason of kinship he was made Pishi Xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianlu era he was appointed Pishi Xiangwen by virtue of his clan ties.

sentences.zh: 二年，與兄劉哥謀反，免死，使於轄戛斯國。

translations.literal: In the second year he plotted rebellion with his elder brother Liuge, was spared death, and was sent to the Kirghiz state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined his elder brother Liuge in rebellion, was spared execution, and was sent to the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 既還，復預察割之亂，陵遲而死。

translations.literal: After he returned, he again took part in Chagai's disorder and died by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he again took part in Chagai's rebellion and was executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 異母弟二人：化葛裏、奚蹇。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers by a different mother: Huagelü and Xijian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two younger half-brothers, Huagelü and Xijian.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，無職任，以族子，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli they held no office; as clansmen they were greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingli era they held no office, but as kinsmen of the imperial clan they were treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 三年，或告化葛裏、奚蹇與衛王宛謀逆，下獄，飾辭獲免。

translations.literal: In the third year someone reported that Huagelü and Xijian plotted treason with Prince Wei Wan; they were imprisoned but escaped by polished excuses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year someone accused Huagelü and Xijian of plotting treason with Prince Wei Wan; they were imprisoned but talked their way free.

sentences.zh: 四年春，復謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year they plotted rebellion again and were executed on confession.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year they rebelled again and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 海思，字鐸袞，隋國王釋魯之庶子。

translations.literal: Haishi, style Duogun, was the secondary son of King of Sui Shilu.
translations.idiomatic: Haishi, whose style was Duogun, was a secondary son of Shilu, King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 機警口辯。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and eloquent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and a gifted debater.

sentences.zh: 會同五年，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huitong an edict sought blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huitong the court issued an edict calling for blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 時海思年十八，衣羊裘，乘牛詣闕。

translations.literal: At that time Haishi was eighteen, wore a sheepskin coat, and came to the palace riding an ox.
translations.idiomatic: Haishi was then eighteen; clad in a sheepskin coat, he rode an ox to the palace.

sentences.zh: 有司問曰：「汝何故來？」

translations.literal: The officials asked, "For what reason have you come?
translations.idiomatic: The officials asked, "Why have you come?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「應詔言事。

translations.literal: He replied, "In response to the edict to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To respond to the edict and speak my mind.

sentences.zh: 茍不以貧稚見遺，亦可備直言之選。」

translations.literal: If I am not rejected for poverty and youth, I may also be fit for the selection of blunt speech."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not dismiss me for being poor and young, I may yet qualify among those chosen to speak plainly."

sentences.zh: 有司以聞。

translations.literal: The officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The officials reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會帝將出獵，使謂曰：「俟吾還則見之。」

translations.literal: As the Emperor was about to go hunting, he sent word saying, "Wait until I return, then you shall be received.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to go hunting and sent word: "Wait until I return, and then you shall be received.

sentences.zh: 海思曰：「臣以陛下急於求賢，是以來耳；

translations.literal: Haishi said, "Your servant came because Your Majesty is eager to seek the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: Haishi said, "I came because Your Majesty is eager to find worthy men;

sentences.zh: 今反緩於獵，請從此歸。」

translations.literal: now you are instead slow for the hunt—your servant asks to return from here."
translations.idiomatic: yet now you put the hunt first. I shall take my leave."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，即召見賜坐，問以治道。

translations.literal: On hearing this, the Emperor at once summoned him, granted him a seat, and questioned him on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he summoned Haishi at once, gave him a seat, and questioned him on the art of government.

sentences.zh: 命明王安端與耶律頗德試之，數日，安端等奏曰：「海思之材，臣等所不及。」

translations.literal: He ordered Prince Ming'an Anduan and Yelü Pode to test him; after several days Anduan and the others memorialized, "Haishi's talent is what your servants cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Prince Ming'an Anduan and Yelü Pode to test him; after several days they reported, "Haishi's ability is beyond what we can match.

sentences.zh: 帝召海思問曰：「與汝言者何如人也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Haishi and asked, "What sort of men were those who spoke with you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Haishi and asked, "What sort of men were those who tested you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安端言無收檢，若空車走峻阪；

translations.literal: He replied, "Anduan's speech has no restraint, like an empty cart running a steep slope;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Anduan's speech has no restraint—it is like driving an empty cart down a steep slope;

sentences.zh: 頗德如著靴行曠野射鴇。」

translations.literal: Pode is like wearing boots to walk the open wilds and shoot bustards."
translations.idiomatic: Pode is like wearing boots to stalk bustards across open country."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 擢宣徽使，屢任以事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and repeatedly entrusted with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and repeatedly entrusted with important duties.

sentences.zh: 帝知其貧，以金器賜之，海思即散於親友。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he was poor and bestowed gold vessels on him; Haishi at once distributed them among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was poor, the emperor gave him gold vessels, which Haishi immediately distributed among his kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 後從帝伐晉有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in the campaign against Jin and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the emperor against Jin and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位於軍中，皇太后以兵逆於潢河橫渡。

translations.literal: Shizong was established in the army; the Empress Dowager opposed him with troops at Huanghe Hengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was proclaimed in the army, the empress dowager marched against him with troops at Huanghe Hengdu.

sentences.zh: 太后遣耶律屋質責世宗自立。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sent Yelü Wuzhi to reproach Shizong for establishing himself on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent Yelü Wuzhi to rebuke Shizong for proclaiming himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 屋質至帝前，諭旨不屈；

translations.literal: Wuzhi came before the Emperor and conveyed the decree without yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhi came before Shizong and delivered the empress dowager's message without yielding;

sentences.zh: 世宗遣海思對，亦不遜，且命之曰：「汝見屋質勿懼！」

translations.literal: Shizong sent Haishi to reply, and he too was not deferential, and moreover ordered him, saying, "When you see Wuzhi, do not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Haishi to answer, and he too was unyielding; Shizong even told him, "When you see Wuzhi, have no fear!

sentences.zh: 海思見太后還，不稱旨。

translations.literal: Haishi saw the Empress Dowager and returned, not to the Emperor's satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Haishi met the empress dowager and returned, having failed to satisfy the emperor.

sentences.zh: 既和，領太后諸局事。

translations.literal: After peace, he oversaw the Empress Dowager's various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, he oversaw the empress dowager's various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，與冀王敵烈謀反，死獄中。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he plotted rebellion with Prince Ji Dilie and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong succeeded, he plotted rebellion with Prince Ji Dilie and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 蕭革，小字滑哥，字胡突堇，國舅房林牙和尚之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Ge, childhood name Huage, style Hutujin, was the son of Guoju-fang Linya Heshang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ge, whose childhood name was Huage and whose style was Hutujin, was the son of Heshang, linya of the Guoju-fang.

sentences.zh: 警悟多智數。

translations.literal: He was alert and possessed many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 太平初，累遷官職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping he was repeatedly promoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping era he rose through a series of promotions.

sentences.zh: 遊近習間，以諛悅相比昵，為流輩所稱，由是名達於上。

translations.literal: Moving among close attendants, he won favor through flattery and drew close to one another; his contemporaries praised him, and thereby his name reached the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Among the emperor's intimates he curried favor with flattery and grew close to them; his peers praised him, and so his name reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，拜北面林牙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he was appointed Northern Linya.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongxi era he was appointed northern linya.

sentences.zh: 十二年，為北院樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he became Vice Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became vice commissioner of the northern bureau of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與近臣宴，謂革曰：「朕知卿才，故自拔擢，卿宜勉力！」

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted with close ministers and said to Ge, "We know your talent and therefore raised you ourselves—you should strive!
translations.idiomatic: At a feast with his intimates the emperor said to Ge, "I know your ability, which is why I promoted you myself—you must do your utmost!

sentences.zh: 革曰：「臣不才，誤蒙聖知，無以報萬一，惟竭愚忠，安敢怠？」

translations.literal: Ge said, "Your servant is without talent yet wrongly received the sage's notice; unable to repay one part in ten thousand, he can only exhaust foolish loyalty—how would he dare be slack?"
translations.idiomatic: Ge replied, "I am without talent yet have wrongly won Your Majesty's favor; I can never repay you in the least, and can only offer my poor loyalty—how could I dare be remiss?"

sentences.zh: 明年，拜北府宰相。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Chancellor of the Northern Administration.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed chancellor of the northern administration.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改同知北院樞密事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was changed to Associate Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made associate commissioner of the northern bureau of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 革怙寵專權，同僚具位而已。

translations.literal: Ge relied on favor and monopolized power; his colleagues held office in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Ge traded on imperial favor and held power alone; his colleagues were mere figureheads.

sentences.zh: 時夷離畢耶律義先知革奸佞，因侍燕，言革所短，用之將敗事。

translations.literal: At that time Yiliebi Yelü Yixian knew Ge's treachery and flattery; attending a banquet, he spoke of Ge's faults, saying that employing him would ruin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yiliebi Yelü Yixian saw through Ge's treachery; at a court banquet he spoke of Ge's faults and warned that putting him in power would ruin the state.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 一日，上令義先對革巡擲，義先酒酣曰：「臣備位大臣，縱不能進忠去佞，安能與賊博乎！」

translations.literal: One day the sovereign ordered Yixian to play pitch-pot against Ge; Yixian, flushed with wine, said, "Your servant holds a minister's post in name only—even if he cannot advance the loyal and remove flatterers, how can he gamble with a traitor!
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor had Yixian play pitch-pot against Ge; Yixian, deep in his cups, said, "I may hold a minister's title in name only, but even if I cannot advance the loyal and drive out flatterers, how can I gamble with a traitor?

sentences.zh: 革銜之，佯言曰：「公相謔，不既甚乎！」

translations.literal: Ge harbored resentment and pretended to say, "Sir, you jest—is it not rather too much!"
translations.idiomatic: Ge nursed a grudge and said with feigned lightness, "Sir, you are only jesting—surely that is going too far!"

sentences.zh: 義先詬詈不已。

translations.literal: Yixian reviled him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian went on cursing him without stop.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，皇后解之曰：「義先酒狂，醒可治也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; the Empress interceded, saying, "Yixian is wild with wine; when sober he may be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, but the empress intervened: "Yixian is drunk and unruly; when he sobers he can be set right.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上詔革謂曰：「義先無禮，可痛繩之。」

translations.literal: The next day the sovereign instructed Ge, saying, "Yixian was rude—you may punish him severely."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor told Ge privately, "Yixian was insolent—you may punish him as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 革曰：「義先之才，豈逃聖鑒！

translations.literal: Ge said, "Yixian's talent—how could it escape the sage's discernment!
translations.idiomatic: Ge replied, "Your Majesty knows Yixian's ability only too well!

sentences.zh: 然天下皆知忠直。

translations.literal: Yet all under Heaven know his loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everyone knows his loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 今以酒過為罪，恐咈人望。」

translations.literal: Now to make a crime of a wine offense may affront public expectation."
translations.idiomatic: To punish him now for a drunken offense would surely disappoint public expectation."

sentences.zh: 帝以革犯而不校，眷遇益厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Ge bore offense without retaliating, favored him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed that Ge had borne the insult without striking back, favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 其矯情媚上多此類。

translations.literal: His feigned sentiment and flattery toward the sovereign were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His feigned devotion and flattery of the throne were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 拜南院樞密使，詔班諸王上，封吳王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs; an edict ranked him above the princes, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner of the southern bureau of military affairs, ranked by edict above the princes, and enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 改知北院，進王鄭，兼中書令。

translations.literal: He was changed to oversee the Northern Bureau, advanced to Prince of Zheng, and concurrently made Zhongshu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to oversee the northern bureau, promoted to Prince of Zheng, and made concurrent zhongshu ling.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，詔革曰：「大位不可一日曠，朕若弗寤，宜即令燕趙國王嗣位。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor grew critically ill, he instructed Ge, "The great position cannot stand vacant for a day; if We do not recover, you should at once have the Prince of Yan and Zhao succeed.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's illness grew grave, he told Ge, "The throne cannot stand empty even for a day; if I do not recover, you should at once have the Prince of Yan and Zhao succeed me.

sentences.zh: 清寧元年，復為南院樞密使，更王楚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingning he again became Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs and was changed to Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingning he again became southern commissioner of military affairs and was retitled Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 復徙北院，與國舅蕭阿剌同掌朝政。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Northern Bureau and, with Guoju Xiao Ala, jointly directed court government.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to the northern bureau and shared control of the government with Guoju Xiao Ala.

sentences.zh: 革多私撓，阿剌每裁正之，由是有隙，出阿剌為東京留守。

translations.literal: Ge often interfered for private ends; Ala repeatedly checked and corrected him, and thereby a rift arose; Ala was sent out as Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Ge often bent affairs to private ends, and Ala repeatedly reined him in; a breach opened between them, and Ala was sent out as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會南郊，阿剌以例赴闕，帝訪群臣以時務，阿剌陳利病，言甚激切。

translations.literal: At the southern suburban sacrifice Ala came to court by precedent; the Emperor questioned the ministers on current affairs, and Ala set forth benefits and harms in speech very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburban rites Ala came to court as custom required; the emperor asked the ministers about current affairs, and Ala spoke out on what helped and harmed the state in terms so forceful they cut deep.

sentences.zh: 革伺帝意不悅，因譖曰：「阿剌恃寵，有慢上心，非臣子禮。」

translations.literal: Ge watched that the Emperor was displeased and slandered him, saying, "Ala relies on favor and shows disrespect to the sovereign's mind—this is not the ritual of subject and lord.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's displeasure, Ge slandered him: "Ala trades on imperial favor and shows disrespect to Your Majesty—this is not how a subject should behave.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，縊阿剌於殿下。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and strangled Ala beneath the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had Ala strangled below the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 後上知革奸計，寵遇漸衰。

translations.literal: Later the sovereign came to know Ge's treacherous schemes, and favor toward him gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor learned of Ge's treachery, and imperial favor toward him gradually faded.

sentences.zh: 八年，致仕，封鄭國王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he left office and was enfeoffed as King of the State of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he retired and was made King of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，革以其子為重元婿，革預其謀，陵遲殺之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year Ge gave his son as son-in-law to Chongyuan; Ge took part in the plot and was killed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year Ge married his son to Chongyuan; Ge took part in the conspiracy and was executed by dismemberment.
